sentences.text:
The petitioner is the 1st accused in S.C.(PMLA) No.5/2025 on the file of the Special Court for PMLA cases/CBI-I, Ernakulam, which has originated from ECIR/KCZO/25/2020 registered against the petitioner and the other accused persons for committing the offences under Section 3 r/w Section 4 of the Prevention of Money Laundering Act, 2002, and for committing the predicate offence under Section 420 of the Indian Penal Code (IPC).
2.
The case of the petitioner is that, the above crime was registered by the respondent on the allegations that the accused persons have committed money laundering.

On the said allegations, Crime No.VC 4/2019 is registered by the Vigilance and Anti-Corruption Bureau, Special Investigation Unit-I,
Thiruvananthapuram, alleging commission of the offences under Section 120B, 409 and 420 of the IPC and Section 13(2) r/w Section 13 (1) (d) of the Prevention of Corruption Act,1988.
3.

The petitioner contends that, he was not granted an opportunity of being heard, before taking cognizance of the said offence, as envisaged under the first proviso to Section 223(1) of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 ('BNSS', for short) and as per the principles laid down by this Court in Saji John v. Assistant Director, Directorate of Enforcement [2025 KHC 819], Therefore,
Annexure-A complaint may be quashed.

entities.text: Saji John v. Assistant Director, Directorate of Enforcement [2025 KHC 819]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
4. I have heard the learned Counsel appearing for the petitioner and the learned Standing Counsel for the 2025:KER:94076 Crl.MC No. 10968 OF 2025 respondent.
5.
The learned counsel for the petitioner submits that, the petitioner is confining his contention in the Crl.M.C, order taking cognizance of the offence without notice to the petitioner.
By Annexure-B order, this Court had quashed the order taking cognizance in respect of accused Nos.2 to 5.
However, in Annexure-B order, this Court has specifically observed that the order will enure to the benefit of the petitioner in Annexure-B order only.
In the above circumstances, the petitioner prays that he may also be afforded an opportunity of being heard.

6. The learned Standing Counsel for the respondent fairly submits that the petitioner was not granted an opportunity of being heard as per the mandate under Section 223(1) of the BNSS before Shelji George vs Directorate Of Enforcement on 4 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/166786909/
2 taking cognizance of the offence.

entities.text: Shelji George vs Directorate Of Enforcement on 4 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 7. In light of the above submission, this Crl.M.C is 2025:KER:94076 Crl.MC No. 10968 OF 2025 allowed, by setting aside the order taking cognizance of the offence in the above crime.

Accordingly,
the Trial Court is directed to reconsider the matter, after affording the petitioner also an opportunity of being heard as envisaged under Section 223(1) of the BNSS.
This Crl.M.C is disposed of accordingly.

Sd/-
